info.name: mpt-extension-sdk mock_app
info.description:
Sample requests for the SDK mock_app running locally on `{{base_url}}` (default `http://localhost:8080`).

Auth is wired automatically:

- A collection-level pre-request script builds a non-prod HS256 JWT from the `extension_id`, `account_id` and `account_type` variables and stores it in `auth_token`.
- Every authenticated request sends `Authorization: Bearer {{auth_token}}` via collection-level Bearer auth (the `ops` requests opt out).

The runtime (mpt-extension-sdk) decodes claims without verifying the signature, so the HS256 dummy secret is only there to produce a structurally valid token. Override `extension_id`, `account_id` or `account_type` in the collection variables to test other identities.

`agreements-sync` is deferrable. Without `MPT-Task-Id` it runs as a direct call. The deferred request starts the call on the devmock, which delivers it with `MPT-Task-Id` as the Extension Service does for a call made with `MPT-Async: true`, so run it against `make run-demo`.

exec: // Build a non-prod HS256 JWT for the local runtime and store it in `auth_token`.
// The runtime decodes claims without verifying the signature, so the dummy
// secret below is fine for local testing only.

request.description: Health report of the running extension. No auth.
Liveness probe. Answers `200 OK` as soon as the process serves requests. No auth.

item.name: ops / ready — readiness probe (200 OK when started, 503 otherwise)

request.description: Readiness probe. Answers `200 OK` once startup has finished and `503` before. No auth.

item.name: event / purchase — supported purchase order (expected OK)

request.description: Delivers an order event to `orders-purchase` directly, as the Extension Framework would. The SDK starts the task, runs `PurchasePipeline` and answers `OK`. Nothing re-delivers it: this request is the whole delivery.
Reads one agreement through the authenticated MPT API service. Answers `200` with the agreement.
The handler raises `NotFoundError` for the id `not-found`, so the SDK maps it to a `404` problem response.
Lists agreements with `offset=2&limit=3`. Answers `200` with the page and the pagination metadata.
`limit=0` asks only for the total. Answers `200` with an empty page and the count.

item.name: API / agreements-sync direct call (expected 204 No Content)

request.description: Calls the deferrable `agreements-sync` without `MPT-Task-Id`, so it runs as a plain API call: the request waits for the sync and answers `204`. No task is involved.

item.name: API / agreements-sync deferred call (expected Defer, then Completed)

request.description:
Starts a deferred call on the devmock (`make run-demo`), which plays the Extension Service for a call made with `MPT-Async: true`.

1. The devmock answers `202` and delivers `POST /api/v2/agreements/sync` with `MPT-Task-Id`.
2. The SDK reads the task, claims it with `execute`, runs the sync in the background and answers `Defer`. The handler writes two task logs and the SDK completes the task.
3. About 30 s later the devmock delivers again; the task reads `completed`, so the SDK answers `OK` and the loop stops.

Sending it again while the first delivery is pending answers `409`; once settled it can be started again.
Creates an agreement from a body that passes `AgreementSchema`. Answers `201` with the created agreement.
The body lacks the fields `AgreementSchema` requires, so the SDK rejects it with `422` before the handler runs.

item.name: schedule / start flow ok (expected Defer, then Completed)

request.description:
Starts the `ok` schedule on the devmock (`make run-demo`).

1. The first delivery is claimed with `execute` and answered `Defer`.
2. The handler logs, reports progress at 50 % and 100 %, and returns; the SDK completes the task.
3. About 30 s later the next delivery reads `completed` and is answered `OK`.

item.name: schedule / start flow cancel (expected Defer, then Failed)

request.description:
Starts the `cancel` schedule on the devmock (`make run-demo`).

1. The first delivery is claimed with `execute` and answered `Defer`.
2. The handler raises `CancelError`; the SDK fails the task.
3. About 30 s later the next delivery reads `failed` and is answered `OK`.

item.name: schedule / start flow timeout (expected Defer, then Failed on deadline)

request.description:
Starts the `timeout` schedule on the devmock (`make run-demo`), and with it the claim scenario.

1. The first delivery reaches the primary (`{{base_url}}`): it claims the task with `execute`, starts a 180 s sleep and answers `Defer`.
2. 5 s later the devmock delivers the same task to `app-secondary` (port 8081). Its `execute` is answered `409`, so it answers `Defer` without running the handler: one task never runs twice.
3. The devmock publishes a 120 s processing budget, so after the SDK's safety margin the primary fails the task on its deadline, in about one minute.
4. The next delivery reads `failed` and is answered `OK`.

Both deliveries schedule their own re-delivery, so two chains run until the task fails.

item.name: schedule / start flow defer (expected repeated Defer)

request.description: Starts the `defer` schedule on the devmock (`make run-demo`). The handler logs a warning and raises `DeferError` on every delivery, so the SDK reschedules the task, which releases the claim, and answers `Defer`. The task never settles, so the devmock delivers it every 30 s until you stop it with `make down`.
